# P36.1b — Crawler conduct text, `robots_policy` field, `/data-collection/` text (R11-GOV-04)

**Requirement ids:** **SIG-INGEST-036 rule 7** (the host-level opt-out the text states is the register P36.1a built — checked before every fetch, before the robots probe, zero egress) · **SIG-INGEST-046c** (the reservation-refused state's public description — refused bytes are never captured, the state is kept distinct from `UNDETERMINED`, and a recorded reservation fails the loader gate outright) · **SIG-INGEST-037**'s restated posture where the text touches it (rule 4 keeps the legal-posture sentence; the counsel clause is waived — WV-07 / ADR-182) · cited: **GL-GATE-08 / ADR-088** (the every-host scope, carried verbatim), **Q-E2-11 [A-5]**, **Q-E2-02 [B-6]**, **SIG-TRANSP-038**, **SIG-ENG-042** (a text claim with no code behind it fails the copy check).

**Ticket:** `docs/tickets/349_P36.1b__crawler-conduct-text-and-robots-field.md` (manifest row 349) · **Base:** `r11/P35.23-real-data-regression-corpus` · **Branch:** `r11/P36.1b-crawler-conduct-text-and-robots-field` · **OM-20 posture:** none — `policy/` text, registry metadata, a copy batch and tests; no production mutation, no live leg, no `ingestion_permitted` flip, no gate ticked. The `/data-collection/` page text rides the next publish.

## Why

E2-07 found the contradiction: `crawler_conduct.toml` rule 2 said "Honor robots.txt … permission is NOT granted", `policy.crawler`'s docstring agreed, the registry carried `robots_policy = "honor"` read as enforcement, and the Stage-0 letter promised "we honour robots/ToS" — while `PoliteFetcher` probes robots, records the verdict, **proceeds** on `disallowed`/`unretrievable` and stamps `robots_disregarded` (GL-GATE-08 / ADR-088; re-confirmed A-5 on every host — ADR-168). Q-E2-02's adopted B-6 line named this fix: bring the four text surfaces in line in one ticket, with a new ADR superseding ADR-088's "accurate declarations" clause and the policy of record published on the crawler page.

## What ships

- **`policy/src/policy/data/crawler_conduct.toml`** — rule 2 retitled "Probe and record robots.txt" and rewritten: RFC 9309 §2.3.1.4 classification (`retrieved` / `no_policy_4xx` / `unretrievable`) recorded on the fetch record (ADR-087), the GL-GATE-08 non-gating posture with `robots_disregarded` + public host + count disclosure, the disallow-is-never-a-reservation clause, the ADR-083 API-mode carve-out and `ingestion_permitted` as the binding gate. Rule 7 names `sig.opt-out-register/1` (checked before every fetch — before even the robots probe — zero egress; an updated register file applies next run, no rebuild or redeploy). Rule 1 names the owned contact URL; rules 4/6 carry the WV-07/WV-09 waiver wording. Version stamp 2026-10-26.
- **`policy/src/policy/crawler.py`** — module + helper docstrings now document the classification-vs-enforcement split: `robots_permits`/`robots_access_permits` produce the *recorded* verdict (they stamp `robots_disregarded`), never gate the fetch; `detect_reservation` and the opt-out register are the refusal paths.
- **`connectors/src/connectors/registry.py` + `sources.toml` header** — `RobotsPolicy` is documented as the source's robots posture **declared at review time**, registry metadata never an enforcement claim (ADR-222): `honor` = "a robots policy governs this crawl surface" read probe-and-record; the closed vocabulary stays verbatim, no row retconned.
- **The ALPR Abuse Library re-record** — `[sources.alpr_abuse_library.rights.reservation]` records the observed `Content-Signal` + Article-4 reservation (kind `content_signal`, verbatim signal, observed 2026-08-20, evidence `docs/research/R2_flock_ecosystem_data_access.md` F2.20). The row stays `ingestion_permitted=false`, `compact_status=not_contacted`, rights `UNDETERMINED` — and the loader gate refuses it under the 046c state even with every other gate field flipped (fixture-verified).
- **`web/src/pages/data-collection.astro`** — the full text replacing P35.38a's minimal page: what SIG fetches and excludes, the UA identity naming the owned contact URL, the eight conduct rules carried **verbatim** (new `CR-01…CR-08` batch rows = `title + ". " + text` from the policy file — the page cannot drift from the policy of record), the robots posture + host+count disclosure, the opt-out register, the reservation refusal distinct from an unresolved review, rate limits/challenge handling, and the `/dispute/` stop route. T0 stays: no `<script>`, no island.
- **Copy batch** — `DC-21` supersedes `DC-03`; `DC-22…DC-32` carry the new sections; every row `pending` (the operator's verbatim confirmation sits under `D-P35.38a-1`, which the batch comment now cites).
- **Stage-0 outreach letter** — the robots/ToS bullet now states the decided posture honestly (probe + record; a disallow does not by itself stop a fetch and is disclosed; a direct opt-out stops us at once; an affirmative reservation is honoured as a refusal). Never sent — sending is operator outreach under ADR-171 (LATER-04).
- **ADR-222** — `robots_policy` declared posture, never enforcement: supersedes ADR-088's "accurate declarations" clause only (status line appended there; the probe-and-record decision stands under ADR-168). ADR index, `ADR_TRIGGERS.csv` register row (quiet at authoring, home BL-086), BL-086 sources + spec Appendix-F row updated; canonical spec regenerated.
- **The copy check** — `tests/unit/test_conduct_text.py` (18 tests): a false-claim lint over the conduct file, docstring, registry header, page rows and letter (the pre-P36.1b texts are flagged); verbatim binding of CR rows to the policy file; and fixture-verified anchors — zero-egress opt-out, a `Disallow` proceeding stamped `robots_disregarded`, a recorded reservation refused at the gate, `host + count` disclosure rows.
